messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered for control-plane dependencies — elevated 5xx from auth + org-lookup. Impacting ~12% of requests across region-us-east-1. Paging SRE oncall.

pagerduty: Trigger: CP_DEP_DEGRADED_HIGH — priority P1 — notify: alice (SRE oncall)

alice (SRE oncall): I'm on it. Can folks who touched control plane configs in the last hour please chime?

jordan (eng): not me, I pushed a small telemetry change earlier but nothing that should affect auth.

mira (platform): I rolled a config for gateway rate windows ~35m ago — low-risk. Reverting seems quick if needed.

carla (controlplane): seeing auth upstream returning 502/504 to our gateway fanout, plus timeouts from org-lookup cache layer. Correlating traces now. Error rate spike started ~1769998700 (20m ago).

alice (SRE oncall): customer-impact: some sign-in and token-verification flows failing; downstream request latencies spiking to >2s and some 5xx. No full outage but user-facing errors.

ben (infra): infra metrics: host CPU on auth pool is normal, but connection saturation to identity-db looks high and a few instances show ephemeral connection queues.

carla (controlplane): logs:
```
auth ERROR: upstream call failed: read timeout after 2s (id=0x7a)
org-lookup WARN: cache-miss spike, falling back to backend, backend returned 504 for 30/120 requests in the last minute
```

alice (SRE oncall): immediate mitigations: 1) open circuit for the failing identity-db shard in the controlplane routing layer, 2) enable retry-with-backoff on gateway for id-lookup calls (small burst), 3) add temporary increased concurrency to org-lookup replicas if autoscaler allows. I'll start 1 and 2.

mira (platform): adding concurrency now for org-lookup group 'org-lookup-us' — will take ~90s.

ben (infra): manually bumped auth pool nodes + added more ephemeral connection slots to the DB proxy. Monitoring connection queues.

alice (SRE oncall): applied routing circuit to identity-db-shard-3 at 1769998805 — traffic diverted to healthy shards. Please confirm no data loss expected, just potential increased latency for users on that shard.

carla (controlplane): confirmed shard 3 removed from fanout, downstream 5xx dropped ~60% in the next 30s. org-lookup errors still present but reduced.

jordan (eng): quick note: gateway retry change rolled to canary at 1769998830; looks like it reduced user-visible errors for a subset of traffic. We'll roll to 50% if stable.

alice (SRE oncall): good. Need to assess root cause: edges: 1) identity-db transient partial degradation; 2) org-lookup backend timeouts possibly caused by cache stampede after eviction; 3) gateway rate window adjustments earlier could have allowed burst.

mira (platform): the gateway config revert is ready if we decide it's contributing. Revert quicker than rolling back runtime controlplane changes.

carla (controlplane): traces show a few hot keys causing cache miss amplification; also a spike of retries from clients at ~1769998725 that amplified load to the DB proxy. We should consider short-term client throttling and longer-term KV caching for hot keys.

alice (SRE oncall): action items (short):
- keep shard circuit open until DB proxy confirms healthy connections (alice)
- finish gateway retry rollout to 50% (jordan)
- keep autoscaler increased for org-lookup while backpressure holds (mira)
- watch user-error rate and page CS for high-severity customers affected (alice)

ben (infra): DB proxy team reports they cleared queued connections and instance mem usage fine now. They'll keep a close eye for next 2 hours.

alice (SRE oncall): customer comms: I'm drafting a short blameless note for support with impacted regions and mitigation steps. @carla please add any specific customer-visible failure patterns.

carla (controlplane): customers hitting token refresh endpoints saw 502, and bulk org API calls experienced timeouts. We'll annotate logs to make search for impacted customers easier: add tag cp_incident_1769998888.

jordan (eng): rolling gateway retry to 50% at 1769998875. If errors continue to fall, we'll go to 100% after +5m check.

alice (SRE oncall): monitoring: error-rate is down ~70% vs peak. Latency p95 improving. Keeping incident open for postmortem and timeline. No paging to broader oncall unless we see degradation again.

deploy-bot: Deploy activity: gateway config update /gateway/rate-window -> reverted canary -> 1769998882 by mira.

mira (platform): revert complete; combined with shard circuit and retry rollout seems stable.

alice (SRE oncall): tentative incident severity: P1 -> degraded to P2 for follow-up (postmortem + mitigation). Please add any config diffs you touched to the incident thread.

carla (controlplane): adding notes: possible cache eviction storm triggered by scheduled maintenance earlier today; we'll run a postmortem to determine exact sequence and propose caching/hot-key mitigations.

ben (infra): follow-up: schedule DB proxy connection limit increase and add more graceful backpressure to controlplane fanout.

alice (SRE oncall): summary for now: - root symptoms: controlplane dependencies (auth DB shard + org-lookup backend) caused elevated 5xx/timeouts; - mitigations: circuit for bad shard, increased org-lookup concurrency, gateway retry rollout, DB proxy connection relief; - customer impact: partial failures for auth/token refresh and org APIs, affecting <5% active users but higher for some accounts; - next: postmortem & action items assigned.

jordan (eng): adding note to runbook: add an explicit step to check DB proxy queues + introduce short-lived per-key caching for org-lookup.

alice (SRE oncall): thanks all. I'll keep the thread open for further telemetry and will mark as incident-closed in ~2 hours if stable.

mira (platform): ACK, will follow up with autoscaler metrics and a short runbook PR.

carla (controlplane): logging tag cp_incident_1769998888 added across controlplane services.

alice (SRE oncall): closing note (1769998950): error rates stable and trending down. Preparing post-incident ticket with timeline and owners. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
